To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
KIR2D4+ NK cells are capable to acquire CCR7 from HLA-Cw3, HLA-Cw5 and HLA-Cwl target cells.

(i) the KIR2D4+ NK cell receptor can induce the acquisition of CCL21 receptor (CCR7) by NK cells after interacting with Cw4 or Cw6 HLA-C molecules; (ii) this process occurs in resting NK cells but it cannot occur in IL-2 activated NK cells due to a down-regulation of IL-18R expression; (iii) the acquisition of CRR7 is not always sufficient in itself to override the inhibition of NK
the recognition of HLA C alleles by the KIR2D4 receptor induces the uptake of Ccr7 by NK cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of a novel function of the KIR receptor, KIR2DS, in the regulation of trogocytic uptake of CCR5 and CCR7 in human NK lymphocytes.
the identification of a new functional consequence of the KIR/HLA interaction.
the role of KIR2D receptors in the regulation of NK cell function and the acquisition of chemokine receptors by KIR2D+ NK cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the KIR2D receptor family, including KIR2DS1 and KIR2DL1, can induce the uptake and the activation of CCR7 on NK cells.
KIR2D molecules can induce the uptake by NK cells of different ligands on the surface of target cells.
the interaction between KIR2DS and HLA-C molecules can result in the activation and functional differentiation of NK cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the KIR2D receptor KIR2DS3 is involved in the regulation of NK cell functions by inducing the uptake of C-C chemokine receptors, such as CCR7.
the KIR2D receptor can induce the uptake by NK cells of a CCR7+ cell expressing certain HLA class I molecules.
the interaction of KIR2D4 with specific HLA-C alleles can induce the acquisition of CRR7 by NK cells and this may be a mechanism to allow NK cells to migrate to the site of inflammation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the interaction between KIR2DS and HLA class I molecules may result in the acquisition of specific receptors by NK cells.
KIR2Ds may play a role in the regulation of the NK cell response by inducing trogocytotic events.
the KIR2DL4/KIR2DS4 system can be exploited as an alternative functional system for investigating the functional outcome of KIR2DL/S recognition of specific HLA class I ligands.
